questions.q: Which of these best defines data governance as used in this course?
options: The system of decision rights, accountability, and rules over how data is created, accessed, and used
A specific software tool for managing databases
The IT department responsible for server uptime
A one-time project to clean up a spreadsheet
questions.explain: Governance is a system of agreements and accountability, not a tool or a single team — the lesson's core definition.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three forces the lesson identifies as making governance unavoidable now?
options: A shortage of office space
Data volume and sprawl across disconnected systems
Regulation such as GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA
AI and automated decisions trained on ungoverned data
questions.explain: The three forces are volume/sprawl, regulation, and AI at scale. Office space isn't a governance driver.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does an organization without governance typically look like?
options: Three teams presenting three different numbers for the same metric in one meeting
A single, obviously broken database that crashes daily
No data stored anywhere in the company
An IT outage that affects the whole company at once
questions.explain: The lesson's examples are quiet, everyday symptoms — like conflicting metrics and shadow spreadsheets — not dramatic outages.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say ungoverned data is a bigger problem for AI than for a traditional report?
options: Because a model repeats the same errors automatically, at scale and speed, with no one reviewing each instance
Because AI models cannot process spreadsheets at all
Because AI always requires more storage than a report
Because regulators specifically exempt AI systems from data rules
questions.explain: A bad number in a report gets noticed by a human; a model trained on the same flaw repeats it automatically across every decision it makes.

questions.q: Per the lesson's roadmap, what does Chapter 2 of this course cover?
options: Named frameworks (like DAMA-DMBOK) and governance operating models
How to write SQL queries
Executive sponsorship specifically
Mock job interviews
questions.explain: Chapter 2, 'Frameworks and Models,' is exactly that — frameworks and operating models, covered in Lessons 7-12.
